candidate.scope: CAP-seq (CXXC affinity purification plus deep sequencing), restricted to the middle row of the supplied Illumina schematic. states.label: CAP-seq DNA reads associated with genomic enrichment profiles
features: The physical readout carrier is the adaptor-bearing library derived from affinity-enriched genomic DNA; it is neither CXXC protein nor a synthetic proxy for RNA.
The primary implementation sequences CAP libraries and maps the DNA reads to the genome. Regional read enrichment identifies DNA rich in clustered unmethylated CpGs.

CAP-seq does not directly measure the methylation state of each sequenced CpG. Lack of enrichment alone does not prove methylation: some unmethylated regions can be inefficiently retained because recovery depends on CpG density and selection stringency.

evidence.locator: Results, Similar abundance and distribution of CpG islands in human and mouse, b00012
evidence.quote: Initial CAP-seq analysis appeared to confirm the lower number of CGIs in mice, but closer examination of syntenic chromosomal regions indicated that the mouse harboured CpG-rich regions that were not efficiently recovered under our CAP conditions (Figure S1A). Bisulfite sequencing established that these regions were in fact unmethylated in the mouse genome and do therefore correspond to potential CGIs (Figure S1B).
evidence.rationale: The paper reports incomplete recovery of some unmethylated regions and relates it to CpG density and selection stringency. Thus absent CAP-seq enrichment alone cannot establish methylation.

operations.label: Hybridize to sepharose column
operations.description: DNA contacts the preassembled CXXC sepharose matrix. Binding retains an enriched subset of fragments containing clusters of unmethylated CpGs and produces matrix-bound DNA. The source calls this “Hybridize to sepharose column”; the primary paper describes protein–DNA affinity binding. The red-site X indicates lack of a methylated-CpG binding contact, not cleavage or demethylation. No separate flow-through branch is drawn.
operations.mechanism: CXXC affinity capture of DNA containing clusters of unmethylated CpGs.
operations.information_effect: Unmethylated-CpG-rich genomic regions become preferentially represented in the retained DNA fraction.

operations.label: Deep sequencing (CAP-seq)
operations.description: The recovered CAP library is used for deep DNA sequencing; the primary implementation maps the resulting reads to the genome to obtain regional enrichment profiles. This broad readout is named in the CAP-seq overview and established by the paper; the sequencer, mapping and routine library-finishing steps are not drawn as separate boxes.
operations.information_effect: Library molecules carry the genomic sequence of the selected fragments. Mapped read enrichment associates CXXC retention with genomic regions containing clusters of unmethylated CpGs. It is a regional affinity-selection readout, with recovery affected by CpG density; it is not direct evidence that every CpG in a retained fragment is unmethylated.

The adjacent G4-seq and CPT-Seq rows are separate targets on the poster, not CAP-seq alternatives. MAP-seq and bisulfite sequencing mentioned in papers are outside this schematic.

corrections.diagram_observation: The diagram labels green dots Unmethylated CpG, places an X under the red methylated-CpG symbol at the matrix, and explicitly labels the recovered material Elute unmethylated CpG enriched fragments. The verified matching collection page nevertheless says “CAP-seq maps methylated CpGs in gDNA” and describes insights into methylated CpG sites.
corrections.primary_statement: Illingworth et al. report CAP enrichment of DNA fragments containing clusters of unmethylated CpGs and identify CAP as the unmethylated-CGI member of reciprocal MAP/CAP maps. The capture operation and readout in this artifact use that primary-supported interpretation, which agrees with the diagram. They do not describe direct positive selection of methylated CpGs.
